chunks: As for the (tribe of) Thamud, We tried to guide them, but they preferred blindness to guidance; then they were seized by the torment of a humiliating punishment as requital for their misdeeds;

key_terms.صَاعِقَةُ الْعَذَابِ: The torment of a thunderbolt/hurrying punishment
key_terms.فَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ: We guided them / We tried to guide them

ai.seo_question: What happened to the tribe of Thamud after they rejected guidance?
ai.summary: This verse highlights the tragic choice of Thamud, who actively preferred spiritual blindness over divine guidance despite receiving clear signs. In Shia exegesis, the 'humiliating thunderbolt' (Saiqah) is often interpreted not merely as a physical event but as a manifestation of divine justice that exposes the inner corruption of those who reject truth. This serves as a timeless warning that punishment is the direct consequence of one's own accumulated deeds (Kasb).
